scenario: A professional typist wants a keyboard that can remain serviceable for a decade and is comparing the current Punkston TK87, RK ROYAL KLUDGE RK100, and CODE V3 listings. They want switch-cycle marketing separated from whole-board durability, long-use owner reports reconciled with counterexamples, and replaceable keycaps, switches, cables, controller or PCB risk considered before any buy-it-for-life recommendation.

rules.current_product_matrix_v1: Compare only frozen body evidence for price, aggregate review display, keycap material or legend method, switch wording, hot-swap compatibility, included replacement parts, and detachable-cable wording. Treat all feature and cycle claims as seller claims, and do not infer an omitted repairability feature.
rules.component_lifetime_scope_v1: A 50-million-cycle statement describes a switch component under an unspecified rating procedure, not the cable, keycaps, sockets, controller, PCB, stabilizers, solder joints, or complete keyboard. Generic metal-contact, debounce, hot-swap, PBT, and doubleshot mechanisms explain failure or replacement boundaries but do not predict a model's service life.
rules.owner_evidence_scope_v1: Use the 11-year Unicomp, four-year NYM96, and approximately 15-year secondhand Logitech G15 records as individual long-use observations. Preserve the Unicomp thread's 18-month, six-year, and roughly 12-year counterexamples and support complaints. Do not convert survivor anecdotes into a population failure rate or transfer them to unrelated shopping models.
rules.repairability_and_spares_v1: Distinguish replaceable wear items from board-level failures. Replacement keycaps and hot-swappable switches can reduce some service risks, while a detachable cable isolates one external failure point. The Sun68 report demonstrates that a failed PCB and unavailable spare can disable an otherwise desirable hot-swap board; therefore hot-swap alone is not whole-board repairability.
rules.evidence_bounded_bifl_decision_v1: No captured current shopping model is proven to last a decade. Among the three current listings, choose the RK100 only as the most repairability-oriented fallback because the seller explicitly states broad 3-pin and 5-pin hot-swap support, includes four replacement switches and a detachable Type-C cable, and uses PBT keycaps; preserve its 77/100 rating over 12 reviews and lack of longitudinal same-model evidence. The CODE V3 isolates cable replacement and advertises gold-plated switches rated at 50 million cycles but does not state hot-swap support and costs $180. The $32 Punkston has an 87/100 rating over 11 reviews and a 50-million-keystroke seller claim but no captured switch- or cable-replacement claim. Treat Unicomp only as the strongest mixed longitudinal reference, not as a captured catalog winner, and recommend verifying PCB availability, warranty, and spare parts before purchase.
